sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers the core Ruby language building blocks that interviewers test in every entry-level Ruby interview. You will learn Ruby's syntax conventions, all variable types (local, instance, class, global, constants), the full range of data types including the critically misunderstood truthiness rules, string operations with interpolation and manipulation methods, arrays and hashes as Ruby's workhorse collection types, symbols and why they exist as a distinct type from strings, all control flow constructs (if/elsif/else, unless, case/when, while, until), method definition with default and keyword arguments, an introduction to blocks and the yield mechanism, and the Enumerable iterator methods that make Ruby collections expressive.

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: Ruby uses snake_case for variables and methods, CamelCase for classes. Only nil and false are falsy — 0, empty string, and empty array are all truthy. Variables: local (name), instance (@name), class (@@name), global ($name), constants (NAME or ClassName). Strings: double quotes allow interpolation #{expr}, single quotes are literal. Symbols (:name) are immutable, interned identifiers — identical symbols share the same object_id. Arrays are ordered and zero-indexed; hashes are key-value stores. Methods return the last evaluated expression implicitly. Blocks are anonymous functions passed to methods using do/end or {}. yield invokes the block passed to a method. Enumerable methods (map, select, reject, find, reduce) transform collections without mutation.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: The most common fresher questions in this module: (1) What is the difference between symbols and strings? (2) What values are falsy in Ruby? (3) Explain the difference between single-quoted and double-quoted strings. (4) What is the difference between puts and print and p? (5) How does yield work? (6) What is the difference between map and each? (7) Write a method that accepts a block and calls it. (8) What is the difference between == and equal?? (9) Explain the difference between while and until. (10) What are the different variable types in Ruby and their scope? These questions appear in almost every screening call for a junior Ruby role.
